treatment.logline: In a monsoon-soaked Colombo minute, a humble vendor and a sheltered daughter meet, spark, and are torn apart by a single phone call.

arc.beat: Set the rain, the stall, and Kasun’s inner drive
arc.feeling: Moody, intimate, hopeful under grey skies

arc.beat: Anudi arrives; fate drops a phone

arc.feeling: Warm, awkward, charming connection amid rain
Jolt, concern, a cloud over warmth

treatment.approach: Keep the world real and tactile: wet asphalt, hiss of rain, tuk-tuks passing soft behind a shallow depth. Let locked-off frames hold the weather while singles isolate emotion. Use one simple move when feeling shifts (a slow creep on Kasun’s thought; a focus rack on the call). Dialogue lives mostly in clean singles with a modest two-shot master as glue. Voices we never see (thought, phone, narrator) are VOs only—no lips moving. Maintain one continuous rain look across the scene.

colour_script.light: Soft overcast, broad bounce; rain highlights

colour_script.grade: Same base; slight lift in saturation on Anudi’s wardrobe

colour_script.grade: Subtle warmth in highlights, clean blacks

treatment.geography: Curbside three-wheeler stall on a Colombo roadside. Stall sits near the curb under a small awning; road and puddles foreground; shopfronts behind. Across the road, a family car pulls up. Dialogue occurs beside the stall at the awning’s edge with rain in frame. Anudi exits downstreet along the pavement; Kasun remains by the stall watching.
treatment.key_image: Rain beads streaking past as Anudi, under her umbrella, faces Kasun—his hair and T-shirt soaked—her world neat and dry, his drenched, a thin line of rain between them.
advice: Never show Father (C03). His voice is phone-only.
Lines marked a thought or heard-not-seen are VO only; no lips moving.
Avoid readable phone screens; show vibration or sound instead.
Keep rain continuity: density, wet wardrobe, droplets on lens consistent.
Protect clean handles (about 1 s in and out) on every clip; keep one move per shot.
Singles carry the dialogue; the two-shot master is glue and rhythm, not coverage for every beat.
Do not add extras or change objects; keep it to the listed place and items.

sequences.title: Rain and resolve
sequences.purpose: Establish rain, stall, and Kasun’s inner ambition (VO thought)

sequences.title: The drop
sequences.purpose: Anudi arrives, drops her phone; Kasun reacts and runs

sequences.title: A smile answers
sequences.purpose: Kasun shares ambition; she smiles back

sequences.title: The cut and the promise
sequences.purpose: Father’s call interrupts; a soft parting; fate VO

moments.what: Heavy rain over Colombo; Kasun works his stall. His determined face carries his private thought (L3) over picture.
moments.feeling: Intimate resolve under harsh rain; we lean into him.
moments.cut_uses: Single MCU on Kasun with a gentle slow creep; establishers as prelude for texture.

moments.what: Across the road Anudi steps out; her phone slips by the stall. Kasun snatches it and runs after her.
moments.cut_uses: WIDE across-road for her entry; INSERT top-down on the drop; MS follow on Kasun’s move.

moments.what: First words: he calls (L7); she turns and thanks (L9); she studies his stall (b10) and asks (L11); warmth grows.
moments.cut_uses: Two-shot MWS master as glue; crisp singles for each speaking line; keep rain texture alive.

moments.what: He speaks his bigger dream (L13). She smiles back, seeing him anew.
moments.cut_uses: Kasun MCU single for L13; quick CU reaction on her smile.

moments.what: Phone rings; Father’s voice (L16) halts the moment. Her face falls; a last look to Kasun.
moments.cut_uses: CU on Anudi with a subtle rack from phone to eyes; optional INSERT of vibrating phone.

moments.what: She bids a soft goodbye (L19) and leaves; Kasun watches in the rain; narrator VO (L22) closes.
moments.cut_uses: Anudi single for the farewell line; clean exit as she walks away; slow creep on Kasun as VO lands.

editor_notes: VO/Thought/Narration: L3, L16, L22 are VO only—never performed on camera.
Dialogue: Prioritize clean singles for L7, L9, L11, L13, L19. Two-shot master glues rhythm and carries ambiance for L7/L9/L11 as alternate.
Motion economy: Only one move per shot (slow creep, follow, rack). Keep other frames locked to honor rain texture.
Umbrella: Use it as frame and divider—never let it hide lips during speaking lines.
Sound bed: Consistent heavy rain with light traffic murmur; leave space in singles for post to ride VO lines.
Continuity: One rain density and wet wardrobe across all clips; ensure matching puddles and droplets on props.
